messages:
maria: heads up — canary rolled at 17:20 UTC and we're seeing ~15% p95 regression on short chats. perf-ci flagged build 2023. looks like a ton of kernels compiling on the backends, latency spikes correspond with compile activity :eyes:
perf-ci-bot: perf-dash: https://perf.redwood/bench/2023 (regression +15% p95, compile-time up x3). CI job `bench/shortseq` failed on canary, logs: https://ci.redwood/logs/2023
ken: linking the deploy: d8f2b6f -> autotune/heuristic-change. That PR tweaked kernel-selection to favor larger fused kernels for throughput. might be picking wrong size for our short-seq traffic
santiago: quick grep of runtime logs shows repeated compile requests for model x86_small@v2: "kernel_compile:start" every ~30s on same host. also kv-cache evictions spike at same time. suspect compile churn invalidating KV cache entries (sequence IDs)
maria: that matches flamegraphs — compilation jitter on the hot path adds wall time and also thrashes kv-cache which forces recompute of prefixes. attaching snippet:
```
flamegraph: runtime_loop -> choose_kernel -> compile_if_needed -> wait_compile (60-80ms spikes)
kv_cache_evictions: 200/s -> 1200/s during spikes
```
elaine: if autotune now prefers the large batch-optimized matmul, compile time is higher and we get cache invalidation because shape/version metadata changes. short requests shouldn't be picked up by that heuristic
ken: i'm working a quick bisect. suspect change in autotune picker at commit 6c7a1e0 (tuned for throughput on long sequences).
ryan: what about rolling back the heuristic only? revert whole PR will be heavy. smaller rollback: pin old kernel-selection policy in canary config and redeploy
santiago: can do a hotfix patch to pin policy to "legacy_small_first". but we need to confirm no other regressions. i can run a targeted bench locally and on canary nodes (will try in 10m)
maria: canary freeze requested — hold larger rollout until we confirm. @deploy-bot please block auto-promote :no_entry_sign:
deploy-bot: Auto-promote blocked on channel request by maria. Can confirm canary freeze applied.
ken: started bisect: testing 6c7a1e0..HEAD. first suspect 6c7a1e0 -> results back in ~15m. early results show compile_count jump introduced there
santiago: local bench after pinning policy shows p95 back to baseline on shortseq. compile_count down to normal. pushing patch `hotfix/pin-legacy-policy` for canary config
elaine: quick note — pinning avoids the new fused kernels, so we lose some throughput on long sequences, but that's acceptable for now until we refine the picker to be sequence-length aware
maria: +1 to pin. can we get a short rollout of just the config change to canary, monitor 30m, then decide revert PR vs fix?
ken: agreed. i'll open an emergency PR to change default to legacy_small_first for canary. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4321
ryan: FYI the memory OOM alerts were correlated with compile surge too. compile temp objects plus kv-cache churn pushed one host near OOM. i've quarantined that host and restarted runtime process
santiago: bisect narrowed it: 6c7a1e0 toggled kernel_weighting to favor fused for shapes < 512. that's the root cause. next: propose selector should consult expected sequence distribution (short vs long) before choosing fused kernels
maria: fine plan. for immediate actions: 1) canary config pin (PR 4321) 2) block rollout (done) 3) follow-up change to selector logic (santiago + ken) 4) postmortem and perf dashboard update (maria)
elaine: i'll review PR 4321 now. quick smoke looks good. please include test that simulates short-seq traffic to prevent regressions in future
ken: putting a hold on merge until smoke passes. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
perf-ci-bot: bench/shortseq (canary) re-run queued by santiago — results will post to perf-dash
maria: assigning owners: santiago (bisect + selector fix), ken (PR + review), elaine (tests), ryan (investigate memory pressure). i'll draft the postmortem after stabilization and link to perf graphs.
deploy-bot: Deploy note: canary freeze active until 1793460380 (unlock by request).
maria: closing thread for now, keeping monitoring channel open. will update in 30m with bench result. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
